title: Spec Traceability Map
description: GAP-020 — binds each requirement to the code that implements it and the test that proves it. The artifact answers the two questions a traceability claim is made of: is everything specified built, and is everything built specified. A map that only answers the first hides scope that nobody asked for.

specRef.description: The requirement — a functional story id, an acceptance criterion, a clause.

implementationRefs.description: Where it is implemented. Empty is meaningful: it says the requirement is not built.

testRefs.description: What proves it. Empty is also meaningful, and worse than the previous one: it says the requirement is built and unverified.

coverage.description: The recomputable verdict for this link. `implemented-untested` and `specified-unimplemented` are named separately rather than lumped into `partial`, because they call for opposite actions.

waiverRef.description: Required when `coverage` is `waived` — otherwise the state is indistinguishable from an omission.

unmappedImplementationRefs.description: Code with no requirement behind it. This is the half of traceability usually left out, and it is where unasked-for scope shows up.
